correctness.rationale: The proof starts with the exact 2^h period of z↦binom(z,a) mod2 and correct suffix-count transitions. An affine permutation-group stabilizer generates all 2^b binary middle-run counter vectors at each zero phase. Explicit same-base opposite-output word pairs cover all b≥2 and even-a b=1 parameters. For odd-a b=1, a pointwise Lucas parity identity determines the final bit. A triangular family of finishing suffixes separates the base vectors, and phase-shift tests separate every zero phase. Two independent programs verified 66 orbit counts, 20 true Moore minimizations, 65,520 direct positional counts, 4,914 witness pairs, 40 injective suffix tests and 877,440 invariant cases. Finite tests support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete infinite two-parameter family of three-run subsequence counters, not a special-case computation or simple parameter substitution. The theorem quantifies exactly when a returning terminal symbol doubles observable memory, gives an exceptional odd/even boundary enforced by a structural Lucas identity, and compresses a naive length-a+b+1 prefix-counter state space to a size logarithmic in a in its exponent. The parity-lift criterion is intrinsic to distinguishing suffixes and can inform more general modular or multi-run minimization problems; no unproved downstream claim is needed for the result to be mathematically useful.
